title: CTS Psalms — Unit 7: Psalm 56, When I Am Afraid

blocks.en: 📖 The Book of Psalms — Unit 7: Psalm 56, When I Am Afraid
blocks.es_reference: 📖 El Libro de los Salmos — Unidad 7: Salmo 56, Cuando Tengo Miedo

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Whenever I am afraid, I will trust in You." — Psalm 56:3 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "En el día que temo, yo en ti confío." — Salmo 56:3 (RVG)

blocks.en: 1. My Father Is in the House
blocks.es_reference: 1. Mi Padre Está en la Casa

blocks.en: When I was a child I had the nightmares that so many children seem to have. I would wake with my heart pounding and my eyes wide open, certain that a monster or a robber had broken into the house. I was terribly afraid. Then I would remember that my father was in the house, and I knew that as long as he was there I did not have to be afraid. And I went back to sleep. That childhood memory holds the whole message of Psalm 56. The psalmist faces real danger, but he has learned where his Father is.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando era niño tenía las pesadillas que tantos niños parecen tener. Despertaba con el corazón latiendo fuerte y los ojos bien abiertos, seguro de que un monstruo o un ladrón había entrado en la casa. Tenía muchísimo miedo. Entonces recordaba que mi padre estaba en la casa, y sabía que mientras él estuviera allí yo no tenía que temer. Y volvía a dormirme. Ese recuerdo de la niñez encierra todo el mensaje del Salmo 56. El salmista enfrenta un peligro real, pero ha aprendido dónde está su Padre.

blocks.en: During the days of the Covenanters in Scotland, believers faced terrible persecution; many were killed and tortured for their faith. Some of them developed a code phrase. When they were stopped and asked where they were going, they would answer, "I am going to my Father's house." It meant more than a journey home. It was a confession that, whatever happened to the body, they belonged to God and were on their way to Him. They had learned to be unafraid because they knew the Father was in the house.
blocks.es_reference: En los días de los Covenanters en Escocia, los creyentes enfrentaron una persecución terrible; muchos fueron muertos y torturados por su fe. Algunos de ellos idearon una frase en clave. Cuando los detenían y les preguntaban a dónde iban, respondían: "Voy a la casa de mi Padre." Significaba más que un viaje a casa. Era una confesión de que, pasara lo que pasara con el cuerpo, pertenecían a Dios e iban camino a Él. Habían aprendido a no temer porque sabían que el Padre estaba en la casa.

blocks.en: 2. Whenever I Am Afraid
blocks.es_reference: 2. En el Día que Temo

blocks.en: Psalm 56:3-4 (NKJV): "Whenever I am afraid, I will trust in You. In God (I will praise His word), in God I have put my trust; I will not fear. What can flesh do to me?"
blocks.es_reference: Salmo 56:3-4 (RVG): "En el día que temo, yo en ti confío. En Dios alabaré su palabra; en Dios he confiado; no temeré lo que el hombre pueda hacerme."

blocks.en: I remember sitting before the television during the Gulf War, watching the live coverage as the conflict began with deadly swiftness. My first reaction was fear. My heart pounded. Men would die, and some commentators were speaking of Armageddon and a world plunged into war. And then I remembered that my Father was in the house, and that I did not have to be afraid. Notice that the psalmist does not say "if" I am afraid, but "whenever" I am afraid — he expects fear to come. The promise is not that the believer never feels afraid, but that in the moment of fear he has somewhere to turn: "I will trust in You." Let us look at four reasons we do not have to be afraid.
blocks.es_reference: Recuerdo estar sentado ante el televisor durante la Guerra del Golfo, viendo la transmisión en vivo cuando el conflicto comenzó con rapidez mortal. Mi primera reacción fue el miedo. Mi corazón latía con fuerza. Hombres morirían, y algunos comentaristas hablaban de Armagedón y de un mundo hundido en la guerra. Y entonces recordé que mi Padre estaba en la casa, y que yo no tenía que temer. Note que el salmista no dice "si" tengo miedo, sino "en el día que temo" — espera que el miedo venga. La promesa no es que el creyente nunca sienta temor, sino que en el momento del temor tiene a dónde volverse: "yo en ti confío." Veamos cuatro razones por las que no tenemos que temer.

blocks.en: 3. The Promises of God
blocks.es_reference: 3. Las Promesas de Dios

blocks.en: First, we do not have to be afraid because of the promises of God. God keeps His promises. He has said, "I will never leave you nor forsake you." In the days of the prophet Amos, Israel was prospering as never before, controlling more territory than at any other time, and the people assumed their wealth was a sign of God's favor. But beneath the prosperity was great sin — oppression of the poor, corruption in the courts, idolatry, and immorality. So Amos warned that God would send them into exile, and He did, by the hand of the Assyrians, whose capital Nineveh stood where Baghdad stands today. Yet even in judgment God promised mercy beyond it. For nearly two hundred years they were captives in a distant land, and surely they wondered whether God had forgotten His promises. But in the end they returned and rebuilt the Temple. Our promise is the same: that "all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are called according to His purpose."
blocks.es_reference: Primero, no tenemos que temer a causa de las promesas de Dios. Dios cumple Sus promesas. Ha dicho: "No te desampararé, ni te dejaré." En los días del profeta Amós, Israel prosperaba como nunca, controlando más territorio que en ningún otro tiempo, y el pueblo suponía que su riqueza era señal del favor de Dios. Pero bajo la prosperidad había gran pecado — opresión del pobre, corrupción en los tribunales, idolatría e inmoralidad. Así que Amós advirtió que Dios los enviaría al exilio, y así fue, por mano de los asirios, cuya capital Nínive estaba donde hoy está Bagdad. Sin embargo, aun en el juicio Dios prometió misericordia más allá de él. Por casi doscientos años fueron cautivos en una tierra lejana, y seguramente se preguntaron si Dios había olvidado Sus promesas. Pero al final regresaron y reconstruyeron el Templo. Nuestra promesa es la misma: que "a los que aman a Dios, todas las cosas les ayudan a bien, a los que conforme a su propósito son llamados."

blocks.en: An elderly Christian lay dying in great distress. "Oh, pastor," he said, "for years I have relied upon the promises of God, but now in the hour of death I cannot remember a single one to comfort me." Knowing that Satan was troubling the man, the preacher answered, "My brother, do you think that God will forget any of His promises?" A smile spread over the face of the dying believer, and he exclaimed, "No, no! He won't! Praise the Lord, now I can fall asleep in Jesus and trust Him to remember them all and bring me safely to heaven." Peace flooded his soul, and a short time later he was ushered into the light of God's eternal day.
blocks.es_reference: Un anciano cristiano yacía moribundo en gran angustia. "Oh, pastor," dijo, "por años me he apoyado en las promesas de Dios, pero ahora en la hora de la muerte no puedo recordar ni una sola para consolarme." Sabiendo que Satanás perturbaba al hombre, el predicador respondió: "Hermano mío, ¿cree usted que Dios olvidará alguna de Sus promesas?" Una sonrisa se extendió por el rostro del creyente moribundo, y exclamó: "¡No, no! ¡No lo hará! Alabado sea el Señor; ahora puedo dormirme en Jesús y confiar en que Él las recuerde todas y me lleve a salvo al cielo." La paz inundó su alma, y poco después fue conducido a la luz del día eterno de Dios.

blocks.en: 4. The Plan of God
blocks.es_reference: 4. El Plan de Dios

blocks.en: Second, we do not have to be afraid because of the plan of God. Ephesians 1:11 says that God "works all things according to the counsel of His will." Job declared, "He makes nations great, and destroys them; He enlarges nations, and guides them." Through all of history nations have risen and fallen, grown strong and been led away captive, yet God has remained upon His throne. And this plan reaches both the great and the small: the Lord who governs the nations has also numbered the very hairs of our head. Someone may object that the world is full of chaos — rising crime, broken homes, gross immorality, weapons enough to destroy the earth many times over. Yet the Bible insists that God has a plan and that He is in control. The world has been in a desperate state before and has survived only because of God's providence. If not for His restraining hand, it would be far worse.
blocks.es_reference: Segundo, no tenemos que temer a causa del plan de Dios. Efesios 1:11 dice que Dios "hace todas las cosas según el consejo de su voluntad." Job declaró: "Él multiplica las naciones, y Él las destruye: Él esparce a las naciones, y las vuelve a reunir." Por toda la historia las naciones han surgido y caído, se han fortalecido y han sido llevadas cautivas, y sin embargo Dios ha permanecido en Su trono. Y este plan alcanza tanto lo grande como lo pequeño: el Señor que gobierna las naciones también ha contado los cabellos mismos de nuestra cabeza. Alguien puede objetar que el mundo está lleno de caos — crimen creciente, hogares rotos, inmoralidad grosera, armas suficientes para destruir la tierra muchas veces. Sin embargo, la Biblia insiste en que Dios tiene un plan y que Él tiene el control. El mundo ha estado antes en un estado desesperado y ha sobrevivido solo por la providencia de Dios. De no ser por Su mano que lo refrena, sería mucho peor.

blocks.en: 5. The Plan of God: No "Ifs" in His World
blocks.es_reference: 5. El Plan de Dios: No Hay "Si" en Su Mundo

blocks.en: Corrie ten Boom and the Shrapnel: When Holland was under attack in the Second World War, Corrie ten Boom lay one night unable to sleep as warplanes growled overhead and artillery shattered the darkness. After a while she heard her sister downstairs and joined her for tea, and they talked through the night until the fighting died away. Stumbling back to her room in the dark, she reached down to pat her pillow and jerked back — something sharp had cut her hand. It was a jagged piece of shrapnel ten inches long, lying exactly where her head would have been. She ran to her sister with it and began, "Betsie, if I hadn't heard you in the kitchen…" But her sister stopped her: "Don't say it, Corrie! There are no 'ifs' in God's world. The center of His will is our safety." In the far harder days of a Nazi prison, Corrie learned that truth again and again: God's will is our hiding place.
blocks.es_reference: Corrie ten Boom y la Metralla: Cuando Holanda era atacada en la Segunda Guerra Mundial, Corrie ten Boom yacía una noche sin poder dormir mientras los aviones de guerra rugían en lo alto y la artillería rompía la oscuridad. Al cabo de un rato oyó a su hermana abajo y se le unió para tomar té, y conversaron toda la noche hasta que los combates cesaron. Tropezando de regreso a su cuarto en la oscuridad, extendió la mano para palmear su almohada y se retiró de golpe — algo afilado le había cortado la mano. Era un pedazo dentado de metralla de veinticinco centímetros, justo donde habría estado su cabeza. Corrió a su hermana con él y comenzó: "Betsie, si no te hubiera oído en la cocina…" Pero su hermana la detuvo: "¡No lo digas, Corrie! No hay 'si' en el mundo de Dios. El centro de Su voluntad es nuestra seguridad." En los días mucho más duros de una prisión nazi, Corrie aprendió esa verdad una y otra vez: la voluntad de Dios es nuestro escondedero.

blocks.en: 6. The Power of God
blocks.es_reference: 6. El Poder de Dios

blocks.en: Third, we do not have to be afraid because of the power of God. "Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding is infinite." Job said, "I know that You can do everything, and that no purpose of Yours can be withheld from You." At God's word the Red Sea divided and stood up like walls; the sun stood still; iron floated on the water; ravens carried food to Elijah; and the lions kept their mouths shut and would not touch Daniel. Men may, in their sin, make decisions outside the will of God, but in the end God's will is done. Nothing can finally stop His plan; one might as well try to hold back a flood with a wall of sand, or turn the stars from their orbits, as to overrule the sovereign will of God.
blocks.es_reference: Tercero, no tenemos que temer a causa del poder de Dios. "Grande es el Señor nuestro, y de mucho poder; y su entendimiento es infinito." Job dijo: "Yo sé que todo lo puedes, y que no hay pensamiento que se esconda de ti." A la palabra de Dios el Mar Rojo se dividió y se levantó como muros; el sol se detuvo; el hierro flotó sobre el agua; los cuervos llevaron comida a Elías; y los leones cerraron sus bocas y no tocaron a Daniel. Los hombres pueden, en su pecado, tomar decisiones fuera de la voluntad de Dios, pero al final la voluntad de Dios se cumple. Nada puede al fin detener Su plan; igual valdría tratar de contener una inundación con un muro de arena, o desviar las estrellas de sus órbitas, que anular la voluntad soberana de Dios.

blocks.en: Consider Pharaoh, who thought his power was supreme and refused to free the Hebrew slaves. The Bible says four times that God hardened Pharaoh's heart, and three times that Pharaoh hardened his own. Who hardened it? Both did — for the same sun that melts the wax also hardens the clay; the heat is the same, but the nature of each is different. Napoleon and Hitler, too, dreamed of ruling the world, yet every power must finally bow to God. Napoleon himself wrote that he knew men, and that Jesus was more than a man — He was God.
blocks.es_reference: Considere a Faraón, que creía que su poder era supremo y se negó a liberar a los esclavos hebreos. La Biblia dice cuatro veces que Dios endureció el corazón de Faraón, y tres veces que Faraón endureció el suyo propio. ¿Quién lo endureció? Ambos — pues el mismo sol que derrite la cera también endurece el barro; el calor es el mismo, pero la naturaleza de cada uno es distinta. Napoleón y Hitler también soñaron con gobernar el mundo, y sin embargo todo poder debe al fin doblegarse ante Dios. El mismo Napoleón escribió que conocía a los hombres, y que Jesús era más que un hombre — era Dios.

blocks.en: 7. The Power of God: The Righteous Seed Preserved
blocks.es_reference: 7. El Poder de Dios: La Simiente Justa Preservada

blocks.en: Satan also has power, and sin can do great damage; if God did not restrain them, the world would be far worse. But Satan has never once been able to thwart God's plan. From the beginning he tried to destroy the Righteous Seed, remembering God's word that the seed of the woman would crush his head. Thinking Abel was the seed, he used Cain to kill him. Centuries later he used Pharaoh to try to drown the seed in Egypt. Because God had said the line would run through David, he used wicked Athaliah to slay every male in David's family — but a nurse hid away the infant Joash, and he lived to become king. He used Herod to kill the children of Bethlehem when Jesus was born.
blocks.es_reference: Satanás también tiene poder, y el pecado puede hacer gran daño; si Dios no los refrenara, el mundo sería mucho peor. Pero Satanás jamás ha podido frustrar el plan de Dios. Desde el principio trató de destruir la Simiente Justa, recordando la palabra de Dios de que la simiente de la mujer aplastaría su cabeza. Pensando que Abel era la simiente, usó a Caín para matarlo. Siglos después usó a Faraón para tratar de ahogar la simiente en Egipto. Porque Dios había dicho que el linaje correría por David, usó a la malvada Atalía para matar a todo varón de la familia de David — pero una nodriza escondió al niño Joás, y vivió para llegar a ser rey. Usó a Herodes para matar a los niños de Belén cuando Jesús nació.

blocks.en: Finally, on the day Jesus died, it seemed that Satan had at last succeeded. We may imagine the demons rejoicing at the cross, certain the Righteous Seed was destroyed. But God had planned every bit of it from the beginning, and on the third day He raised Jesus from the dead. The divine plan is fixed; there can be no deviation from it and no destroying it. "Forever, O LORD, Your word is settled in heaven." The very moment that looked like Satan's victory was the hour of our salvation.
blocks.es_reference: Finalmente, el día que Jesús murió, pareció que Satanás al fin había triunfado. Podemos imaginar a los demonios regocijándose ante la cruz, seguros de que la Simiente Justa había sido destruida. Pero Dios lo había planeado todo desde el principio, y al tercer día resucitó a Jesús de los muertos. El plan divino es fijo; no puede haber desviación de él ni destrucción de él. "Para siempre, oh Jehová, permanece tu palabra en los cielos." El mismísimo momento que parecía la victoria de Satanás era la hora de nuestra salvación.

blocks.en: 8. The Protection of God
blocks.es_reference: 8. La Protección de Dios

blocks.en: Fourth, we do not have to be afraid because of the protection of God, who "upholds all things by the word of His power." A few centuries ago many people, including some of America's founders, held to Deism — the belief that God set the world in motion and then stepped back, leaving it to run like a great machine without His further involvement. If that were true, then God is not active now, prayer is useless, and the world is simply drifting toward chaos. But the Bible tells us the opposite: God upholds all things, and He calls us to pray, even for those in authority over us, whether or not we agree with them, for they need His wisdom. Men are sinful and make mistakes, sometimes terrible ones — yet God can take even the mistakes of men and still accomplish His purposes. God always knows what is best. Even if we knew every fact, we could not make every right decision; but God can. When we pray, God already knows our need, and He answers by giving what is best.
blocks.es_reference: Cuarto, no tenemos que temer a causa de la protección de Dios, quien "sustenta todas las cosas con la palabra de su poder." Hace algunos siglos muchos, incluidos algunos de los fundadores de los Estados Unidos, sostenían el deísmo — la creencia de que Dios puso el mundo en marcha y luego se apartó, dejándolo correr como una gran máquina sin Su intervención posterior. Si eso fuera cierto, entonces Dios no está activo ahora, la oración es inútil, y el mundo simplemente va a la deriva hacia el caos. Pero la Biblia nos dice lo contrario: Dios sustenta todas las cosas, y nos llama a orar, aun por los que tienen autoridad sobre nosotros, estemos o no de acuerdo con ellos, pues necesitan Su sabiduría. Los hombres son pecadores y cometen errores, a veces terribles — y sin embargo Dios puede tomar aun los errores de los hombres y cumplir Sus propósitos. Dios siempre sabe lo que es mejor. Aunque conociéramos cada hecho, no podríamos tomar cada decisión correcta; pero Dios sí puede. Cuando oramos, Dios ya conoce nuestra necesidad, y responde dándonos lo que es mejor.

blocks.en: As Long as God Is Awake: A mother and her little four-year-old daughter were getting ready for bed. The child was afraid of the dark, and the mother, alone with her that night, felt fearful too. When the light went out, the child caught sight of the moon through the window. "Mother," she asked, "is the moon God's light?" "Yes," said the mother. "Will God put out His light and go to sleep?" "No, my child," the mother answered, "God never goes to sleep." Then out of the simplicity of a child's faith came the words that gave the fearful mother her own assurance: "Well, as long as God is awake, there's no sense in both of us staying awake." Whenever you are afraid, remember that your Father is in the house, and He never sleeps. Trust in Him.
blocks.es_reference: Mientras Dios Esté Despierto: Una madre y su pequeña hija de cuatro años se preparaban para dormir. La niña temía la oscuridad, y la madre, sola con ella esa noche, también sentía temor. Cuando se apagó la luz, la niña alcanzó a ver la luna por la ventana. "Mamá," preguntó, "¿es la luna la luz de Dios?" "Sí," dijo la madre. "¿Apagará Dios Su luz y se irá a dormir?" "No, hija mía," respondió la madre, "Dios nunca se duerme." Entonces, de la sencillez de la fe de una niña, vinieron las palabras que dieron a la madre temerosa su propia seguridad: "Bueno, mientras Dios esté despierto, no tiene sentido que las dos nos quedemos despiertas." Cuando tenga miedo, recuerde que su Padre está en la casa, y nunca duerme. Confíe en Él.

mc.stem: What childhood memory does the lesson use to open Psalm 56?
options: Waking from a nightmare and remembering his father was in the house
mc.why: The lesson opens with waking from a nightmare and being calmed by remembering father was in the house.

mc.stem: What code phrase did the Scottish Covenanters use when asked where they were going?
options: "I am going to my Father's house"
mc.why: The Scottish Covenanters' code phrase was 'I am going to my Father's house' — a confession of belonging to God.

mc.stem: The preacher recalls his own fear at frightening news on television. What point does he draw from it?
options: That bad news should be ignored
That even amid frightening events the believer need not fear, for his Father is near
That Christians are exempt from danger
mc.why: Even amid frightening events the believer need not fear, because his Father is near and in control.

mc.stem: According to Psalm 56:3, what does the psalmist do "whenever" he is afraid?
mc.why: Psalm 56:3 gives the believer's response to fear: 'Whenever I am afraid, I will trust in You.'

mc.stem: What is significant about the psalmist saying "whenever" rather than "if" I am afraid?
options: He expects fear to come, and has somewhere to turn in it
He claims he is never afraid
He is speaking only of others
mc.why: 'Whenever' (not 'if') means fear will come — but the believer always has Someone to turn to in it.

mc.stem: The lesson gives four reasons not to fear. Which set is correct?
options: His silence, sleep, distance, and delay
The promises, plan, power, and protection of God
mc.why: The lesson gives four reasons not to fear: the promises, the plan, the power, and the protection of God.

mc.stem: In the days of Amos, why did the people wrongly assume God favored them?
options: Because they were prospering and controlled much territory
Because the Temple was newly built
mc.why: In Amos' day the people wrongly assumed prosperity meant God's favor, while ignoring their great sin.

mc.stem: What striking geographical note does the lesson make about Assyria's capital, Nineveh?
options: It became the city of Athens
It stood where Baghdad stands today
mc.why: Strikingly, Assyria's capital Nineveh stood where Baghdad stands today — God's word touches real history.

mc.stem: In the story of the dying Christian, what comforted him when he could not remember a single promise?
options: The thought that God would not forget any of His promises
mc.why: The dying Christian who forgot every promise was comforted by one thought: God would not forget any of His promises.

mc.stem: Which verse does the lesson cite to show that God's plan reaches even the smallest things?
options: The very hairs of our head are numbered
Be still and know that I am God
mc.why: God's plan reaches even the smallest things — the very hairs of our head are numbered.

mc.stem: The Corrie ten Boom story, where shrapnel lay exactly where her head would have been, is used to teach what?
options: That we should fear sleeping near windows
That there are no accidents in God's world; the center of His will is our safety
That God protects only the famous
mc.why: Corrie ten Boom's shrapnel story teaches there are no accidents in God's world; the center of His will is our safety.

mc.stem: What did Betsie tell Corrie when she began to say "if I hadn't heard you in the kitchen"?
options: "There are no 'ifs' in God's world; the center of His will is our safety"
mc.why: Betsie's words capture it: 'There are no ifs in God's world; the center of His will is our safety.'

mc.stem: According to the lesson, how can both God and Pharaoh be said to have hardened Pharaoh's heart?
options: The same sun melts wax and hardens clay; the heat is the same but the nature differs
God forced Pharaoh against his will
Pharaoh acted entirely apart from God
It was only a figure of speech
mc.why: The same sun melts wax and hardens clay: God and Pharaoh both hardened his heart, the difference lying in Pharaoh's nature.

mc.stem: What did Napoleon himself reportedly write about Jesus, according to the lesson?
options: That He was only a great teacher
That he knew men, and that Jesus was more than a man — He was God
That religion was for the weak
That he had never heard of Him
mc.why: Napoleon wrote that he knew men, and that Jesus was more than a man — He was God.

mc.stem: The lesson traces Satan's repeated attempts to destroy the "Righteous Seed." Which sequence is given?
options: Cain killing Abel, Pharaoh, Athaliah (but Joash hidden), and Herod
mc.why: Satan tried again and again to destroy the Righteous Seed — through Cain, Pharaoh, Athaliah, and Herod — and failed every time.

mc.stem: What does the lesson say about the day Jesus died, when Satan seemed to triumph?
options: It proved God's plan had failed
It showed Satan's power was greater
God had planned it all, and raised Jesus on the third day
mc.why: The day Jesus died looked like Satan's victory, but God had planned it all and raised Jesus on the third day.

mc.stem: What belief, held by some of America's founders, does the lesson identify and reject?
options: Deism — that God set the world in motion and then stepped back
mc.why: Deism — that God set the world going and then stepped back — is rejected; God upholds and is active in His world.

mc.stem: According to the lesson, what should we do regarding those in authority over us?
options: Pray for them, for they need God's wisdom
mc.why: We are told to pray for those in authority, for they need God's wisdom — whether or not we agree with them.

mc.stem: What does the lesson say God can do even with the mistakes of sinful men?
options: He can take them and still accomplish His purposes
mc.why: God can take even the mistakes of sinful men and still accomplish His purposes — nothing escapes His plan.

mc.stem: In the closing story, what did the four-year-old say that comforted her fearful mother?
options: "As long as God is awake, there's no sense in both of us staying awake"
mc.why: The four-year-old's words say it best: 'As long as God is awake, there's no sense in both of us staying awake.'

sa.prompt: Explain the childhood memory and the Covenanters' code phrase the lesson uses to open Psalm 56, and what they teach about fear.
sa.model: The lesson opens with a child waking from a nightmare, frightened until he remembers his father is in the house, and with the Scottish Covenanters, who, when asked where they were going, answered, "I am going to my Father's house." Both teach the same truth about fear: the believer is never alone or unprotected, because the Father is near. Fear loses its grip not when danger disappears but when we remember whose house we are in and who watches over us. Psalm 56 is built on that confidence, that even in the night of fear our Father is present.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that the psalmist says "whenever" rather than "if" I am afraid? What is the promise of Psalm 56:3?
sa.model: Psalm 56:3 says, "Whenever I am afraid, I will trust in You." The word "whenever" rather than "if" is significant: the psalmist does not pretend he might escape fear. He expects fear to come, as it comes to everyone, but he has settled in advance where he will turn when it does. The promise is not that the believer will never feel afraid, but that fear can become a trigger for trust. Each time fear rises, it can send us straight to God rather than into panic. Fear is real, but it always has somewhere to go: into the hands of a trustworthy God.

sa.prompt: Explain the first reason not to fear: the promises of God. Use the example of Amos and Israel's exile.
sa.model: The first reason not to fear is the promises of God: He has bound Himself by His word, and His promises do not fail. The lesson uses Amos and Israel to warn the other way too, for the people presumed on God's favor while ignoring their sin, and exile came as God had said. God's promises are sure both to comfort and to warn; what He says, He does. For the believer this is solid ground: we need not fear the future, because the God who cannot lie has promised to be with us, to keep us, and to bring His purposes to pass.

sa.prompt: What does the account of the dying Christian who could not remember a single promise teach about resting in God's faithfulness?
sa.model: The lesson tells of a dying Christian who, in his last hours, could not call a single promise of Scripture to mind, and was distressed by it, until he was comforted by the thought that even if he could not remember God's promises, God would never forget them. The point is that our security does not rest on the strength of our memory or our faith but on God's own faithfulness. When we are too weak, sick, or frightened to hold on to God, He still holds on to us. We can rest, not because we keep every promise in view, but because the God who made them keeps them all.

sa.prompt: Explain the second reason not to fear: the plan of God. How does it reach both the great and the small?
sa.model: The second reason not to fear is the plan of God, which is so complete that it reaches both the great and the small. God governs the rise and fall of nations, yet Jesus said the very hairs of our head are numbered and not a sparrow falls without the Father. Nothing is too large to be outside His control or too small to escape His notice. For the fearful believer this is deep comfort: the same God who directs all history is attentive to the smallest detail of my life. I am not at the mercy of chance, but held within a wise and loving plan.

sa.prompt: What do Corrie ten Boom's shrapnel experience and Betsie's words teach about God's will and our safety?
sa.model: During an air raid, Corrie ten Boom found a jagged piece of shrapnel lying exactly where her head would have been on her pillow. When she began to say, "If I hadn't been delayed in the kitchen," her sister Betsie stopped her: "There are no 'ifs' in God's world; the center of His will is our safety." The account teaches that what looks like chance is held within God's sovereign care, and that the safest place to be is the center of His will, whatever it holds. Our security is not the absence of danger but the presence and purpose of God surrounding every moment.

sa.prompt: Explain the third reason not to fear: the power of God. Give examples of His power from Scripture.
sa.model: The third reason not to fear is the power of God, who is able to do all He has promised. Scripture is full of His power: He created the world by His word, parted the sea for Israel, shut the mouths of lions for Daniel, and raised Jesus from the dead. The God who holds such power is the God who has pledged to keep us. Fear shrinks when we remember that no enemy, circumstance, or force is stronger than the One who watches over us. His promises are not empty wishes; they are backed by the limitless power of the Almighty.

sa.prompt: Explain Pharaoh's hardened heart using the lesson's image of the sun, and what it shows about God's power and human will.
sa.model: The lesson explains Pharaoh's hardened heart with the image of the sun: the same sun that melts wax also hardens clay; the heat is identical, but the result depends on the nature of the thing it shines on. So Scripture can say both that God hardened Pharaoh's heart and that Pharaoh hardened his own, for God's same dealings soften a humble heart and harden a proud one. This shows God's power working without erasing human responsibility. The God of all power is sovereign over Pharaoh, yet Pharaoh's hardness is truly his own; both are fully true at once.

sa.prompt: Trace how Satan repeatedly tried to destroy the Righteous Seed and how God preserved His plan, ending at the cross and resurrection.
sa.model: The lesson traces how Satan tried again and again to destroy the "Righteous Seed," the promised line leading to Christ: Cain killed Abel, Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew boys killed, Athaliah tried to destroy the royal line but the child Joash was hidden, and Herod slaughtered the infants of Bethlehem. Every attempt failed, because God preserved His plan. Even the day Jesus died, when Satan seemed to win, God had planned it all and raised Jesus on the third day. The whole history shows that no scheme of the enemy can overturn God's purpose; the plan that runs to the cross and resurrection cannot be stopped.

sa.prompt: Explain the fourth reason not to fear: the protection of God. Why is Deism rejected, and what does the story of the moon teach?
sa.model: The fourth reason not to fear is the protection of God, who does not set the world going and then walk away. The lesson rejects Deism, the belief that God wound up the universe like a clock and then stepped back, because Scripture shows a God who upholds and watches over His world at every moment. The story of the child who said, "As long as God is awake, there's no sense in both of us staying awake," captures it: God never sleeps, so the believer can rest. We are not left to fend for ourselves; we are kept through the night by a God who is always present and always watching.
